# ClientX

> ClientX is a library for typed, declarative HTTP API clients on Python 3.12+, built on httpx2 and Pydantic v2. You declare endpoints as decorated methods with empty bodies; ClientX builds each request from the method's signature and annotations and decodes the response into the declared return type. It can also describe a client's endpoints as AI tools and serve them over MCP.

Install with `pip install clientx`, or `pip install "clientx[mcp]"` for the MCP server. ClientX depends on `httpx2`, which is a different package from `httpx`: import `httpx2`, not `httpx`.

A complete client:

```python
from typing import Annotated

from clientx import Body, ClientX, DumpConfig, PathParam, Query, Resource, Response, method
from clientx.decoders import ModelDecoder, TypeAdapterDecoder
from pydantic import BaseModel, TypeAdapter


class User(BaseModel):
    id: int
    name: str


class NewUser(BaseModel):
    name: str


class UserChanges(BaseModel):
    name: str | None = None


class Users(Resource, prefix="/users", tags=["users"]):
    @method.get("/{user_id}", decoder=ModelDecoder(User))
    def retrieve(self, user_id: Annotated[int, PathParam(description="The user's ID")]) -> User:
        """Fetch one user by ID."""
        ...

    @method.get(decoder=TypeAdapterDecoder(TypeAdapter(list[User])))
    def search(self, name: Annotated[str, Query("q")], limit: Annotated[int | None, Query()] = None) -> list[User]:
        """Search users by name."""
        ...

    @method.post(decoder=ModelDecoder(User))
    def create(self, payload: NewUser) -> User:
        """Create a user."""
        ...

    @method.patch("/{user_id}", decoder=ModelDecoder(User))
    def update(
        self, user_id: int, changes: Annotated[UserChanges, Body(dump_config=DumpConfig(exclude_unset=True))]
    ) -> User:
        """Change some of a user's fields."""
        ...

    @method.delete("/{user_id}")
    def remove(self, user_id: int) -> None:
        """Delete a user."""
        ...


class ExampleAPI(ClientX):
    users = Users()

    @method.get("/health")
    def health(self) -> Response:
        """Check the service."""
        ...


# A 4xx or 5xx response raises httpx2.HTTPStatusError from any endpoint (raise_for_status=False turns it off).
with ExampleAPI("https://api.example.com", auth=("user", "secret"), timeout=10.0) as api:
    user = api.users.retrieve(42)  # GET /users/42 -> User
    matches = api.users.search("Ada")  # GET /users?q=Ada -> list[User] (limit is None, so it's left out)
    api.users.create(NewUser(name="Ada"))  # POST /users with JSON {"name": "Ada"}
    api.users.update(42, UserChanges(name="Ada L."))  # PATCH /users/42 with JSON {"name": "Ada L."}
```

Rules for writing endpoints:

- Endpoint bodies never run. Write `...`, after the docstring if there is one: pyright rejects a body that's only a docstring when the return type isn't `None`. Decorate endpoints with `@method.get(...)`, after `from clientx import method`; the module `clientx.method` has `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`, `head` and `options`. Each takes `path` (default `""`: the base URL, or a resource's prefix itself, so `@method.get()` in a `prefix="/users"` resource is `GET /users`), and optionally `decoder`, `deprecated` (for example `DeprecatedMessage("...")`), `tags`, `timeout`, `raise_for_status`, and `validate_arguments` (each `True`/`False`, overriding the client's).
- The parameters build the request, and the return type describes the response: a model in the return type is decoded from the response and is never sent. Every endpoint needs a return annotation. `-> Response` (`clientx.Response` is `httpx2.Response`; `clientx` also re-exports `Auth`, `Request` and `Timeout`) returns the raw response, `-> None` returns nothing, and any other type requires `decoder=`. Type checkers check that the decoder's output matches the annotation: a typed return without a decoder is reported as not assignable to the type variable `ResponseOrNone`, and a mismatched decoder as an incompatible callable (ignore mypy's note about positional-only arguments). A missing annotation or decoder raises when the class is defined.
- Decoders, from `clientx.decoders`: `ModelDecoder(Model)`, `TypeAdapterDecoder(TypeAdapter(T))` (it takes a `TypeAdapter`, not a bare type; `key="results"` validates that member of a JSON object instead of the whole body), `FromResponseDecoder(Model)` (calls `Model.from_response(response)`), `json_decoder` (returns `Any`), `text_decoder`, `content_decoder`, or any callable `(httpx2.Response) -> T`. A 4xx or 5xx response raises `httpx2.HTTPStatusError` before the decoder runs; otherwise a decoder always runs when given. A decoder's exception reaches the caller unchanged: `ModelDecoder`, `TypeAdapterDecoder` and `json_decoder` raise `ValueError` subclasses (`pydantic.ValidationError`, `json.JSONDecodeError`, or `ValueError` for a missing `key`), and the DEBUG log record, written before decoding, shows the response's status and no error.
- `{placeholders}` in the path are filled from parameters with the same names, including placeholders in a resource prefix. Values are converted like query values (an `Enum` becomes its value) and percent-encoded as one segment, so `/` `?` `#` and `..` in a value can't change the path. Use `{name:path}` to keep slashes in a value such as a file path; any other converter raises `PathTemplateError`. A `None` or empty value, or a `{name:path}` value with a leading, trailing, or doubled slash, raises `PathValueError` before sending, since it would call a different path. Don't pre-encode values: `%` would be encoded again.
- Each other parameter goes to the first of these that matches: (1) its name is a request part (`params`, `json`, `data`, `files`, `headers`), which wins even over an annotation, so a parameter named `data` is always form data; (2) a request-part annotation: `Annotated[T, Query()]` (query parameters), `Header()`, `Form()` (form data), `Body()` (JSON body), or `File()` (multipart files); (3) its value is a Pydantic model, which is expanded field by field (fields annotated with a helper go to that part, the rest to the JSON body). Anything else raises `UnconsumableArgumentError`. Arguments for the same part merge in parameter order, and later ones win silently (dicts key by key; any other value replaces the part).
- `Query`, `Header`, and `Form` take an optional `key`, the name to send under: `Query("userId")`. Without it, a single value (str, int, Enum, list) is sent under the parameter name, and `Header()` turns underscores into hyphens (`request_id` becomes `request-id`). A list repeats the name (`?tag=a&tag=b`). A mapping or model is merged into the part. Model fields follow the same rules, under their alias or field name. `Body()` and `File()` take no key; on a model field they merge the value into that part, so it must be a mapping or a model, and anything else (`None` included) raises `UnconsumableArgumentError`.
- `None` is never sent as a query parameter, header, or form field, so optional parameters work as `Annotated[int | None, Query()] = None`; pass `""` to send an empty value. A JSON body keeps `null`. Values become JSON-compatible: an `Enum` its `.value`, a `datetime` ISO 8601, a `UUID` a string; numbers and booleans in headers become text.
- Models are dumped with `mode="json"` and `by_alias=True`, so fields are sent under their aliases (`Field(alias="userId")` or `alias_generator=to_camel`): don't add `serialize_by_alias`. Every helper takes `dump_config=DumpConfig(...)`, whose keys override those defaults and go to `model_dump`: `exclude_unset=True` (only the fields that were set, for PATCH), `exclude_none`, `exclude_defaults`, `include`, `exclude`, `by_alias`, `mode`, `context`, `round_trip`, `serialize_as_any`, `exclude_computed_fields`, `warnings`. A JSON body that's a list or dict of models (`json: list[User]`, or `Annotated[list[User], Body()]`) is dumped the same way, and a `RootModel` parameter is the whole JSON body.
- Reuse annotations with `type` aliases: `type UserId = Annotated[int | None, Query("userId")]`. A helper applies to the whole parameter or field: one helper, in the outermost `Annotated`, around the full type with `None` inside (`Annotated[int | None, Query()]`, `QueryParam[int | None]`). A helper nested inside another type (`Annotated[int, Query()] | None`, `list[Annotated[str, Query()]]`) or a second helper raises `MisplacedHelperError`. If the part depends on the value's type, write separate endpoints. Only ClientX helpers must be outermost: Pydantic metadata may be nested, so an ID-or-name path parameter is `Annotated[Annotated[int, Field(ge=1)] | Annotated[str, Field(pattern=...)], PathParam(description=...)]`.
- The helpers are named like FastAPI's but build the outgoing request. In a FastAPI app, import ClientX's under another name (`from clientx import Query as ClientQuery`) or use `clientx.Query(...)`.
- Streaming: `StreamLinesDecoder()` and `StreamChunksDecoder(chunk_size=...)` with `-> Iterator[str]` / `-> Iterator[bytes]` stream the body and release the connection when iteration ends. `StreamResponseDecoder()` with `-> Response` returns the open response, which the caller must read or close. For `async def` endpoints, use `AsyncStreamLinesDecoder()`, `AsyncStreamChunksDecoder(chunk_size=...)`, or an `AsyncStreamDecoder` subclass (an `async def __call__` that yields), with `-> AsyncIterator[str]` / `-> AsyncIterator[bytes]`, and iterate with `async for line in await api.events()`: awaiting raises for a 4xx or 5xx before iteration, and the connection is released when iteration ends, fails, or the iterator is closed (or garbage-collected, if you stop early). A stream decoder for the other kind of endpoint raises `EndpointSignatureError` when the class is defined.
- Resources group endpoints: `class Users(Resource, prefix="/users", tags=[...])`, mounted as an instance (`users = Users()`) on a `ClientX` subclass or on another resource. Prefixes are absolute (they're not combined when nesting); put an API-wide prefix such as `/v1` in the base URL. Resource tags come before each endpoint's tags. Calling a resource that isn't mounted raises `UnboundResourceError`.
- Clients and resources can have plain, undecorated methods: they aren't endpoints or tools, and they call endpoints through `self`. Use them to normalize arguments (endpoint bodies never run, and validation never converts) and for pagination: a `next` URL can't be passed back as a path value, which is percent-encoded, so read its query parameters with `httpx2.URL(next).params` and call the list endpoint.
- An endpoint's name hides any other meaning of that name for the rest of the class body. With bare imports (`from clientx.method import get`), a method called `get` replaces the decorator, so a later `@get(...)` fails when the class is defined; `@method.get(...)` can't be hidden that way. A method called `list` (or `dict`, `type`, ...) makes a later `list[Post]`, in an annotation or a decorator argument, fail when the class is defined with `TypeError: 'function' object is not subscriptable` (pyright reports it too). Define that method last in the class, or write `builtins.list[Post]` after it (`import builtins`).
- Names `ClientX` itself uses can't be endpoint or resource names on a `ClientX` subclass: `close` and dunder methods raise `EndpointNameConflictError`. They're free on a `Resource`. `send` is free on both. On an `AsyncClientX`, `aclose` is reserved too, and `close` is free.
- mypy reports `empty-body` for `...` bodies with a non-`None` return type. Turn that code off for client modules (`# mypy: disable-error-code="empty-body"`); pyright accepts `...`.

Using clients:

- `ClientX(base_url=None, user_agent=None, raise_for_status=True, validate_arguments=False, **kwargs)` forwards every other keyword to `httpx2.Client`. A client class can ship defaults as class arguments, `class ExampleAPI(ClientX, base_url="https://api.example.com", user_agent="example-api/1.0")`, so `ExampleAPI()` needs no arguments; arguments given when creating the client win, and a subclass keeps its parent's. `base_url` and `user_agent` are the only class arguments: any other keyword in the class statement raises `TypeError: ...__init_subclass__() takes no keyword arguments`, so pass other options when creating the client. Without a base URL in either place, creating the client raises `TypeError`. The `User-Agent` is the `user_agent` argument, else one in `headers=`, else the class's, else `ClientX/<version>`. The keywords include `auth`, `headers`, `params`, `cookies`, `timeout`, `verify`, `cert`, `proxy`, `transport`, `mounts`, `event_hooks`, `follow_redirects`, and so on. Close a client with `with` or `close()`. `with` is optional: a long-lived client (web app, worker, MCP server) is created once, reused for every request, and closed with `close()` at shutdown; a closed client can't be reused (`RuntimeError`). Settings can't be changed after the client is created; to use different ones, create another client. Instances are independent, each with its own connections, settings and credentials; class arguments are only defaults. There's no method for sending a raw request: to call a URL the client has no method for, add an endpoint.
- Async: subclass `AsyncClientX` (on `httpx2.AsyncClient`, with the same arguments, class arguments and options) and write endpoints as `async def` methods with the same decorators. `await api.users.retrieve(42)` returns the decoded value, and `asyncio.gather(api.users.retrieve(1), api.users.retrieve(2))` sends requests concurrently over the client's connections. Group async endpoints with `AsyncResource`, which mounts only on an `AsyncClientX` or another `AsyncResource`. An `async def` endpoint on a `ClientX` or `Resource`, a `def` endpoint on an `AsyncClientX` or `AsyncResource`, a resource mounted on the other kind, or a class that subclasses both kinds raises when the class is defined, and type checkers report it at the decorator. Close with `async with` or `await client.aclose()`. `transport=` and `mounts=` take async transports (`httpx2.MockTransport` serves both kinds), and event hooks must be `async` functions. Test with anyio's pytest plugin, which comes with httpx2: `@pytest.mark.anyio async def test_...`.
- Authentication: pass credentials with `auth=` when creating the client, never as endpoint parameters. `auth=` is httpx2's authentication option; for what it accepts and how to write an `Auth` subclass (such as OAuth 2 client credentials), see https://pydantic.dev/docs/httpx2/advanced/authentication/. Don't add credentials in a request event hook: hooks are for logging, and a request hook runs again for each redirect, putting back the `Authorization` header httpx2 drops for another host. Use a third-party library's `Auth` class, not its `httpx2.Client` subclass: ClientX creates its own client.
- Status codes: a 4xx or 5xx response raises `httpx2.HTTPStatusError` from every endpoint, with the body already read (`exc.response.json()` works) and before any decoder runs. Redirects aren't errors: with `follow_redirects=True` only the final response is checked, and without it a 3xx is returned. A streamed error response is read and closed before raising. Turn it off for a client with `ClientX(..., raise_for_status=False)`, or per endpoint with `@method.get(..., raise_for_status=False)` (the endpoint's setting wins), for example to return a 404 as a `Response` or to let a decoder handle error statuses. Don't add a `raise_for_status` decoder or event hook.
- Argument validation is opt-in: `ClientX(..., validate_arguments=True)`, or `@method.get(..., validate_arguments=...)` per endpoint (the endpoint's setting wins). It checks each argument the caller passes against its full annotation (including `Field` constraints) in Pydantic's strict mode, before sending, and raises `ArgumentValidationError` (`.parameter`, `.validation_error`). Values are never converted (`"1"` doesn't match `int`), defaults aren't checked, and types Pydantic can't validate (such as `BinaryIO`) are skipped.
- Test clients without the network: `ExampleAPI(transport=httpx2.MockTransport(handler))`, where `handler(request: httpx2.Request) -> httpx2.Response` records each request (assert on `request.method`, `request.url.path`, `request.url.params`, `request.headers`, `request.content`) and returns the response to decode, or a 4xx to test `HTTPStatusError`. Test an MCP server in memory with `async with mcp.Client(create_mcp_server(client)) as session: await session.call_tool(name, arguments)`.
- Errors all derive from `clientx.ClientXError`. When the class is defined: `MissingReturnTypeError`, `MissingDecoderError`, `EndpointNameConflictError`, `MissingPathArgumentsError` (a path or resource-prefix placeholder that names no parameter), `PathTemplateError` (a converter other than `{name:path}`), `EndpointSignatureError` (no positional first parameter for the client, a `*args`/`**kwargs` parameter, an endpoint of the wrong kind for its class, or a stream decoder for the other kind of endpoint), and `MisplacedHelperError` (for a model field, when the class is defined if a parameter is annotated with the model, or else when it's sent). At call time: `UnconsumableArgumentError`, `PathValueError`, `UnboundResourceError`, and `ArgumentValidationError` when validation is on. Annotations are evaluated when the class is defined, so `from __future__ import annotations` works; types they name must be module-level. HTTP errors come from httpx2: connection errors, timeouts, and `HTTPStatusError` for 4xx and 5xx responses.
- Logging: one DEBUG record per endpoint call on the `clientx` logger, such as `ClientX request: GET /users/42 -> 200 in 12.3 ms (Users.retrieve)` (or `-> 404 HTTPStatusError`), with attributes `clientx_endpoint`, `clientx_method`, `clientx_path`, `clientx_parts`, `clientx_stream`, `clientx_status`, `clientx_elapsed_ms`, and `clientx_error`. It never contains header values, bodies, or query strings; the path does include path parameter values, so keep secrets out of them. httpx2 separately logs each request at INFO on the `httpx2` logger. For custom request logging, pass httpx2 `event_hooks`.
- To list a client's endpoints for docs or tooling, use `clientx.tools.list_tools(client)` (below): name, method, full path, tags, docstring and schemas, including resources. There's no global endpoint registry, and `Endpoint` isn't public.

AI tools and MCP:

- `clientx.tools.list_tools(client, read_only=False, include_tags=None, exclude_tags=(), include_deprecated=False)` returns one `Tool` per endpoint, including resources: `name` (attribute path with underscores, such as `users_retrieve`), `description` (the docstring), `input_schema` and `output_schema` (JSON Schema), `read_only` / `destructive` / `idempotent` (from the HTTP method: GET, HEAD and OPTIONS are read-only; PUT, PATCH and DELETE are destructive; POST is neither and isn't idempotent; GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT and DELETE are idempotent), `method`, `path`, `tags`, and `deprecated`. `tool.call(arguments)` validates the arguments and calls the endpoint through the client, returning a JSON-friendly result; errors propagate, including `HTTPStatusError` for 4xx and 5xx responses (the MCP server turns them into error results with the status, method, path and start of the body, never the host or query string). An `HTTPStatusError`'s own message has the full URL, so don't send `str(error)` to a model if the client puts credentials in query parameters. `read_only=True` keeps only GET, HEAD and OPTIONS endpoints. Streaming endpoints are left out. An `AsyncClientX`'s tools have `is_async` set: call them with `await tool.acall(arguments)` (`call` raises `TypeError` for them, and `acall` for a sync tool).
- `clientx.mcp.run_mcp_server(client, *, name=None, instructions=None, read_only=True, include_tags=None, exclude_tags=(), include_deprecated=False)` serves those tools as an MCP server over stdio (it needs the `mcp` extra). Unlike `list_tools`, it defaults to `read_only=True`: pass `read_only=False` to serve POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE endpoints too. Tools carry `readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint` and `openWorldHint` annotations. `create_mcp_server(...)` takes the same arguments and returns the low-level `mcp.server.lowlevel.Server` for other transports. Don't print to stdout in an MCP server process. It serves a `ClientX` or an `AsyncClientX`: an async client's tools are awaited on the server's event loop, and a sync client's run in a worker thread.
- Docstrings become tool descriptions. Describe a parameter with the helper's `description=`: `Annotated[int | None, Query("userId", description="...")]`, or `Annotated[int, PathParam(description="...")]` for a path parameter (`PathParam` only describes; a `PathParam()` parameter without a placeholder in the path, prefix included, raises `EndpointSignatureError` when the class is defined, and `PathParam` on a model field raises `MisplacedHelperError`). A description goes into the parameter's or field's JSON Schema (so into tool and MCP schemas, and a model's `model_json_schema()`) and never changes the request. `pydantic.Field(description=...)` also works and wins if both are given. Keep credentials in the client's `auth=`, never in endpoint parameters, which models see and fill in.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/slatecipher/ClientX/blob/mainline/README.md): overview, install, and a quickstart
- [Defining endpoints](https://github.com/slatecipher/ClientX/blob/mainline/docs/endpoints.md): verb decorators and their options, empty method bodies and mypy, deprecation
- [Resources](https://github.com/slatecipher/ClientX/blob/mainline/docs/resources.md): path prefixes, nesting, plain methods for pagination and normalizing arguments
- [Return types and decoders](https://github.com/slatecipher/ClientX/blob/mainline/docs/decoders.md): ModelDecoder, TypeAdapterDecoder (including key=), FromResponseDecoder, simple decoders, your own, streaming
- [Building requests](https://github.com/slatecipher/ClientX/blob/mainline/docs/requests.md): how parameters become the path, query string, headers, form fields, JSON body, and files
- [Client configuration](https://github.com/slatecipher/ClientX/blob/mainline/docs/configuration.md): creating and closing a client, class defaults for base_url and user_agent, authentication (auth=, with links to httpx2's auth docs), errors for 4xx and 5xx, argument validation
- [Async clients](https://github.com/slatecipher/ClientX/blob/mainline/docs/async.md): AsyncClientX and AsyncResource for async def endpoints, concurrent requests, async streaming, AI tools, testing
- [Logging](https://github.com/slatecipher/ClientX/blob/mainline/docs/logging.md): ClientX's debug records and your own request logging
- [AI tools and MCP](https://github.com/slatecipher/ClientX/blob/mainline/docs/ai-tools.md): clientx.tools, serving a client over MCP, listing a client's endpoints
- [Testing](https://github.com/slatecipher/ClientX/blob/mainline/docs/testing.md): MockTransport, testing tools, and an in-memory MCP server
- [Errors](https://github.com/slatecipher/ClientX/blob/mainline/docs/errors.md): every error ClientX raises, and when
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/slatecipher/ClientX/blob/mainline/CHANGELOG.md): changes in each release; the API may change between minor versions before 1.0

## Examples

- [Beeceptor example client](https://github.com/slatecipher/ClientX/tree/mainline/examples/beeceptor): a complete client with resources, model decoders, and a deprecated endpoint, run by `examples/beeceptor_example.py`
- [JSONPlaceholder example client](https://github.com/slatecipher/ClientX/tree/mainline/examples/jsonplaceholder): a client for a real public API with the request-part helpers (`Query("userId", description=...)`, `Body` with `exclude_unset` for PATCH), `PathParam(description=...)` with `Field(ge=1, le=100)` bounds for path parameters (checked before sending when `validate_arguments=True`), camelCase aliases, and a 404 caught as `httpx2.HTTPStatusError`, run by `examples/jsonplaceholder_example.py` (it needs network access)
- [OAuth 2 example client](https://github.com/slatecipher/ClientX/tree/mainline/examples/oauth2): an `Auth` subclass that gets a bearer token with a client ID and secret (OAuth 2 client credentials), reuses it until it expires and renews it after a 401, used as `auth=` against Duende's public demo server, with a request hook that only logs; run by `examples/oauth2_example.py` (it needs network access)
- [Async JSONPlaceholder example](https://github.com/slatecipher/ClientX/blob/mainline/examples/jsonplaceholder_async_example.py): an `AsyncClientX` with `AsyncResource`s for the same API (`examples/jsonplaceholder/jsonplaceholder_async_client.py`), fetching data one request at a time and concurrently with `asyncio.gather` (it needs network access)
- [AI tools example](https://github.com/slatecipher/ClientX/blob/mainline/examples/beeceptor_tools_example.py): the same client's endpoints as AI tools, with definitions, schemas, filters, and calls
